title: Former U.S. Marine Released From Russian Detention After Four Years
dek: Robert Gilman, a former U.S. Marine, has been released after more than four years in Russian detention. The Trump administration stated he was freed on humanitarian grounds. The circumstances of his detention and the specifics of his release remain unclear.
author: The GoCheckMyNews Desk
key_fact: Robert Gilman, a former U.S. Marine, has been released from Russian detention after over four years.
bottom_line: Gilman's return home marks a notable prisoner release during ongoing U.S.-Russia tensions, though key details about his detention, the reasons for his release, and any underlying negotiations remain unconfirmed. Clarity on these points may come as the full account of his case emerges.
body: Robert Gilman, a former U.S. Marine, has been released from Russian detention after more than four years, according to NPR reporting on August 12.
The Trump administration said Gilman was freed on humanitarian grounds, according to NPR's reporting.
Supporters had raised concerns about Gilman's health during his detention, per NPR reporting.

The circumstances that led to Gilman's detention in Russia, the specific health concerns that prompted the humanitarian grounds claim, and whether any negotiation or prisoner exchange was involved in his release remain unclear from the available record. Russia has not publicly commented on the release.
